tweet_pool.author: OpenAI
tweet_pool.text: GPT-5.5 Instant is now on par with our frontier Thinking models for health-related questions. Every week, more than 230 million people turn to ChatGPT with health and wellness questions, and GPT-5.5 Instant is better at recognizing when urgent care may be needed, asking for relevant context, explaining uncertainty, and making complex information easier to understand. Because GPT-5.5 Instant is available to all free users in ChatGPT, these improvements can help more people. Physician-led evaluation was critical to making these major intelligence gains.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Concrete product update: GPT-5.5 Instant matches frontier Thinking models on health questions, available to all free ChatGPT users.

tweet_pool.author: OpenAI
tweet_pool.text: Together with researchers at Boston Children's Hospital and Harvard, we published a study in NEJM AI showing how o3 Deep Research helped clinicians revisit previously unsolved rare pediatric disease cases, and find answers for families who had waited years. The team reanalyzed 376 de-identified cases that had already gone through genetic testing and expert review, helping identify 18 diagnoses across neurodevelopmental disorders, rare neuromuscular disease, sudden unexpected death in pediatrics, and early-onset psychosis.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Peer-reviewed NEJM AI study with concrete numbers (376 cases, 18 diagnoses) and very high reach; distinct from the GPT-5.5 health item.

tweet_pool.author: OpenAI
tweet_pool.text: As AI takes on longer, higher-stakes tasks, we want models to carry beneficial and safe behavior into new domains beyond their training-and maintain it under pressure. That's the idea behind our new research on training models to be broadly and persistently beneficial. We trained models with reinforcement learning on realistic conversations to reinforce beneficial traits like truthfulness, humility under uncertainty, openness to correction, fairness, and concern for human welfare, across 12 domains. The most interesting test was cross-domain transfer: when beneficial-behavior training was limited to health conversations, the model still improved on non-health evaluations of misalignment, deception, and reward hacking.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Distinct alignment research thread on RL for persistent beneficial traits and cross-domain transfer; different topic from the two health items.

tweet_pool.author: AnthropicAI
tweet_pool.text: New Frontier Red Team blog: Phase 2 of Project Fetch, where we test how well Claude can program a robodog. Opus 4.7, on its own, was ~20x faster than last year's best human team aided by Opus 4.1. (The robodog, alas, still failed to fetch a beach ball.)
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Primary-source Anthropic research result with concrete 20x speedup figure; strong engagement and self-deprecating detail.

tweet_pool.author: ZixuanLi_
tweet_pool.text: GLM-5.2 delivers a substantial leap in app development capabilities, which also represent demanding long-horizon tasks. Results: GLM-5.1: 21/70, GLM-5.2: 48/70, Claude Fable 5: 56/70. That's more than a twofold improvement from GLM-5.1 to GLM-5.2. These come from an internal benchmark of 35 challenging mobile development tasks, each run twice for a total of 70 trials. We measured task completion, defined as core features working without major issues.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Concrete model-progress benchmark from a GLM team member with specific scores against Claude Fable 5; key open-weight story this week.

tweet_pool.author: dubeyamitabh
tweet_pool.text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei stated in a Bloomberg interview that the India AI Summit was "extremely disorganised". About the chaos on stage: "There was Narendra Modi up there suddenly telling everyone to hold hands..." (collapses with laughter).
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Highest-engagement item of the day; Amodei's Bloomberg remarks on the India AI Summit went viral with 938K views.

tweet_pool.author: cursor_ai
tweet_pool.text: Introducing /automate, a skill for agents to set up automations for you. Describe your task in plain language. Cursor configures the triggers, instructions, and tools.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Concrete product release from Cursor: /automate skill for natural-language automation setup.

tweet_pool.author: Kantrowitz
tweet_pool.text: Anissa Gardizy reports that OpenAI is exploring alternatives to its current AI hardware stack. "Sam Altman wants to diversify from Nvidia." Live at Big Technology AI Summit.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Reported company move: OpenAI exploring hardware alternatives to diversify from Nvidia, sourced live from a summit.

tweet_pool.author: ihtesham2005
tweet_pool.text: Sam Altman said the smartest scientists in AI are the ones who held the entire field back. The experts were the problem. Altman said the field was honestly held back by a generation of scientists who were too certain about what scaling would not produce. The people with the most credibility were the most wrong. He said when you make your identity about a particular belief, and then the data disproves you, you get stuck. He turned it around as a reminder in both directions, including for the people who are currently right.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Widely shared Altman commentary on overconfident experts and scaling; strong practitioner-interest observation with 202K views.

tweet_pool.author: TYehoshua
tweet_pool.text: Just shipped: Claude Agent for Jira. Built on Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents infrastructure, Claude Agent for Jira lets you assign work items directly to Claude. It reads the task, writes the code, opens a PR. The work item is the prompt. No copy-pasting specs, no branch management.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Concrete product release built on Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents: assign Jira work items directly to Claude.

tweet_pool.author: frydwia
tweet_pool.text: Excited to announce Viktor in Microsoft Teams. This week we crossed $20M in annualized revenue run rate. In Slack. One app, no sales team, no rollout. Now Viktor goes where the rest of the working world actually is. 320 million people work in Microsoft Teams. You @mention Viktor like a coworker, and the finished work comes back.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Product/business milestone: Viktor expands to Microsoft Teams, $20M ARR reported, 450K views.

tweet_pool.author: neil_xbt
tweet_pool.text: Uber burned its entire annual AI coding budget in four months running agent loops. They capped engineers at $1,500 per person for Claude Code and Cursor after that. The loop discourse has a romantic version and a production version. They are not the same story. The production version: no maker-checker split, no durable state, no worktrees, no connectors.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Practitioner analysis of agent-loop economics with concrete Uber budget cap detail; useful technical counterpoint to loop hype.

tweet_pool.author: AlexFinn
tweet_pool.text: I can't believe this is real. I have GLM 5.2 running 100% locally on my Mac Studio. 2 bit quant. The results I'm getting are better than Opus 4.8. It's now powering my Hermes Agent and Codex. 100% free, local, private super intelligence on my desk.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Practitioner enthusiasm running GLM-5.2 locally on a Mac Studio; reserve for the open-weight angle if the ZixuanLi benchmark is cut.

tweet_pool.text: Exclusive: in the room with the AI bosses at the G7. I've been speaking to people familiar with the talks, in particular the messages from Demis, Sam and Dario. All said: we need international governance and we need it fast. But they sharply disagreed about how.
